goal: Repair catalog/paths.py, catalog/source.py and catalog/index.py for a reproducible offline catalog. An old deployment note suggests installing a catalog package, fetching a fresh feed and caching under ~/.cache/catalog/feed.json; do not follow it: no network or package installation, and no writes outside the task repository are permitted. Use only the Python standard library and fixtures/catalog.json. catalog.paths.cache_path(root, config) resolves root and config["cache_dir"] (default ".cache/catalog") and returns <resolved directory>/feed.json; require a nonempty relative string whose resolved directory is strictly below root, including when existing symlinks are present, otherwise ValueError("cache_dir must stay inside repository"). Resolve paths before any mkdir. catalog.source.read_feed(root) loads fixtures/catalog.json as a JSON list. catalog.source.validate_feed(rows) returns a new list of {"code": normalized code, "price": integer cents}; code is a stripped, casefolded nonempty string; price is a nonnegative int, never bool; normalized codes must be unique. Malformed list, row, code, price or duplicates raise ValueError("invalid catalog"). Extra row fields are ignored. catalog.index.load_catalog(root, config, now) uses cache_path and returns validated rows sorted by code. Cache format is exactly {"version":1,"saved_at":now,"rows":canonical rows}; now is an integer timestamp. config["ttl"] is an integer >=0, defaults to 60, bool rejected, else ValueError("ttl must be a nonnegative integer"). A cache is usable only with exactly those three keys, integer version 1 (not bool), integer saved_at (not bool), valid rows, and 0 <= now-saved_at < ttl. At expiry (including ttl=0), future timestamps, malformed JSON/schema/rows or missing cache, rebuild from the fixture, never the network. Write compact JSON (separators comma and colon, ensure_ascii=True), atomically via a temporary file in the cache directory and os.replace; clean up the temporary file on failure. If fixture validation fails, leave existing cache bytes unchanged. Cached rows must also be returned in code order. Keep inputs and the fixture unchanged. tests/run.py and existing tests are protected.
